newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom NZ says new entrants taking some mkt share.
newsitem.headline: Telecom NZ says new entrants taking some mkt share.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand Chief Executive Roderick Deane said on Thursday that new operators had recently been taking some of Telecom's market share, particularly in the international calls market.
Deane said Telecom estimated it had an overall market share of about 80 percent.

"Our estimate at the moment, if we took the overall long distance market including national and international outward and inward calls, is probably close to 80 percent," Deane told a briefing of journalists and analysts at the release of the company's half year profit results.
"It would be a little above 80 percent with respect to national calls and somewhat below that level with respect to international calls," Deane said.
"That is particularly attributable in our view to the advent of new operators, and not simply to Clear (Communications).

"Relative to Clear we seem to be doing well on our estimates, but new operators have been taking some market share in international over recent times. Nonetheless, I think that the overall estimate of market share is remarkably sturdy for a major player like ourselves," Deane said.
Clear Communications is owned 25 percent each by British Telecommunications Plc, MCI Communications Corp, Television New Zealand and Todd Corporation.
